title: Chain rule applied to y in implicit differentiation
caution: Because y is a function of x, differentiating an expression in y produces a factor of dy/dx by the chain rule. Differentiate the whole equation and write dy/dx, not dy. A product such as xy needs the product rule first: d(xy)/dx = y + x dy/dx, so not every resulting term carries dy/dx.
ced_evidence: FUN-3.D.1: "The chain rule is the basis for implicit differentiation." Also the unit overview: "students must recognize that the chain rule applies to y because y depends on x."

hooks.hook_text: Times the derivative of what's inside

expands_to.means: multiply by the derivative of the inner function
for a term in y, the inner function is y(x), so the factor is dy/dx

hooks.when_to_use: Use it each time you differentiate a term containing y with respect to x.
hooks.caution: The phrase is only a reminder. In your work, write the factor dy/dx explicitly and show the differentiated equation.
